marks.gloss_en: on the version 'not made by human hands is no partition': it is made by human hands [so it is a partition]
תנן: העושה סוכתו בין האילנות ... כשרה -- והא קאזיל ואתי! the trees sway back and forth, yet they are valid walls
הכא במאי עסקינן -- בקשין: hard trees (= p_okimta_kashin)
the stam: the mishnah speaks of hard [trees, that do not sway]
והאיכא נופו! -- even hard trees have foliage, which sways
דעביד ליה בהוצא ודפנא -- he fastened it with palm fronds and laurel
what the mishnah teaches: we do not decree against [such a sukkah] lest one come to use the tree [on the festival]
תא שמע: היה שם אילן או גדר או מחיצת הקנים -- נידון משום דיומד! a reed partition, which sways, counts
התם נמי, משום דעביד ליה בהוצא ודפנא
if there was a tree, a fence or a partition of reeds there, it is judged as a double-post [of the well enclosure]
תא שמע: אילן המיסך על הארץ ... מטלטלין תחתיו -- אמאי, הא קאזיל ואתי?
התם נמי, דעביד ליה בהוצא ודפנא (= p_okimta_ilan_hutza)
a tree that spreads down over the ground: if its foliage is not three tefachim above the ground, one may carry beneath it

אי הכי, ניטלטל בכוליה! אלמה אמר רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: אין מטלטלין בו אלא בית סאתים? -- if the foliage was fastened, carrying should be permitted in all of it (an amoraic-memra contradiction; kind svara under protest, header)
Rav Huna brei deRav Yehoshua: one may carry in it [beneath the spreading tree] only [if it is] two beit se'ah
one who makes his sukkah between the trees, and the trees are its walls -- it is valid
Rav Acha bar Yaakov: any partition that cannot stand in a common wind is not a partition
סלקא דעתך אמינא: הואיל ואיתקש יציאה להויה, מה הויה בכסף אף יציאה בכסף -- since leaving [marriage] is juxtaposed to becoming [married], as becoming is by money so leaving would be by money
קא משמע לן: ״וכתב״ -- she is divorced by writing and not by money
the Rabbis use 'and he shall write' for: she is divorced by writing, and is not divorced by money
מאי טעמיה דרבי יוסי הגלילי? דתניא ... מה ספר דבר שאין בו רוח חיים ואינו אוכל -- so a get may not be written on a living thing (bare דתניא; tanya_kevatei per the Sukkah siblings' convention)
in R' Yosei HaGelili's name they said: nor may women's bills of divorce be written on it (on the living thing of the earlier baraita -- the antecedent is Steinsaltz's rendering)
כדתניא: על מנת שלא תשתי יין ... לעולם -- אין זה כריתות; כל שלשים יום -- הרי זה כריתות
the Rabbis need 'scroll of severance' for: [the get must be] a thing that severs between him and her
the baraita: if so, why does it say 'scroll'? to tell you: as a scroll is a thing without life and not food, so any thing without life and not food
the Rabbis: had it written 'in the scroll', it would be as you say; now that it writes 'scroll', it comes merely for an account of matters
R' Yosei HaGelili derives it from 'a scroll of severance': a scroll severs her, and nothing else severs her
R' Yosei HaGelili derives [the severing-thing requirement] from 'karet' written as 'keritut'
